_comment:
Arrive fast, overshoot the mark, snap back onto it. The OVERSHOOT is the skid — there is no skid clip and there does not need to be one: a whole-actor move that carries the character PAST where they were supposed to stop, followed by a hard un-eased snap back, is what the eye reads as brakes. Everything else is dressing: speedlines on the way in, a scrape and a puff of smoke at the feet on the stop, a two-swing body wobble to bleed off the momentum.

Deliberately NOT animated: legs, feet, any run cycle. Limited animation never draws the run — it draws the lean and lets the speedlines do the running. This is pure tier 1-3 (whole-actor move + camera shake + two effects + two guaranteed sounds + ad-hoc `body` transforms + two of the six faces), so it casts on every rig that will ever exist, with no new art and no rig authoring.

On `dx`: like a role's `at` block, a move's dx/dy are offsets from the mark the role was BOUND to, not accumulations — which is why the last move is `dx: 0.0` and not a mirror of the ones before it. Position carries to the end of the SCENE, so ending anywhere but 0.0 would leave the character permanently shoved sideways two shots later.

beats._comment: the run has to start somewhere off the mark. Reposition while HIDDEN so the audience never sees the teleport — 0.30s of cover is nearly 4 frames at 12fps, comfortably enough for the move to land before anyone is looking.
the speedlines ARE the run. No legs are drawn.

0.28s of standing there visible before this is the anticipation — 'here they come'. The lean SNAPS (parts do not tween) which is right: a run lean is a held attitude, not a transition. Sign convention does not matter, because the read comes from the REVERSAL at 0.92, not from which way this leans.

the charge. It travels from -0.62 to +0.28, i.e. 0.28 PAST the mark — the overshoot is baked into the arrival, so the skid costs nothing extra. Eased, so it decelerates into the overshoot the way a slide does.
dust at the FEET, not at the head — dy near zero
the brace: the body slams back the other way while the feet keep sliding. This reversal is the whole gag and it must POP, which is exactly what a parts transform does.
back onto the mark. Deliberately NOT eased — an eased return is a graceful glide, and this needs to be a recoil.
wobble past vertical — momentum bleeding off in decreasing swings, 0.20s apart so each one is a visible 2-3 frames
empty transform set = back to the rig's own rest pose. This is the tidy-up rule 5 demands.
the button: they stopped, and only now do they register what they stopped for
